title.zh: 卷二十 列傳第一 皇后
title.raw: 卷二十 列傳第一 皇后 Volume 20 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷二十‧列傳第一

translations.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 20 — Biographies 1
translations.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 20 — Biographies 1

sentences.zh: 六宮位號，漢、魏以來，因襲增置，世不同矣。

translations.literal: The ranks of the six palaces, from Han and Wei onward, were inherited and augmented; each age differed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace ranks in the six inner quarters, from Han and Wei on, were carried forward and added to—no two reigns alike.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，有司奏置貴嬪、夫人、貴人爲三夫人，脩華、脩儀、脩容、淑妃、淑媛、淑儀、婕妤、容華、充華爲九嬪，美人、中才人、才人爲散職。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 1: the relevant offices memorialized establishing Noble Consort, Lady, and Honored Person as the Three Ladies; Cultivated Elegance, Cultivated Comportment, Cultivated Bearing, Pure Consort, Pure Lady, Pure Rite, Talented Lady, Radiant Splendor, and Fulfilling Splendor as the Nine Consorts; and Beauty, Middle Talent, and Talent as miscellaneous posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 the relevant offices proposed the Three Ladies—Noble Consort, Lady, and Honored Person—and the Nine Consorts: Cultivated Elegance, Cultivated Comportment, Cultivated Bearing, Pure Consort, Pure Lady, Pure Rite, Talented Lady, Radiant Splendor, and Fulfilling Splendor, with Beauty, Middle Talent, and Talent as unattached offices.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，有司奏貴妃、淑妃竝加金章紫綬，佩于窴玉。

translations.literal: Yongming year 1: the relevant offices memorialized that Honored Consort and Pure Consort alike should receive gold seals and purple cords and wear Khotan jade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 1 the relevant offices proposed that Honored Consort and Pure Consort alike receive gold seals and purple cords and wear Khotan jade pendants.

sentences.zh: 淑妃舊擬九棘，以淑爲溫恭之稱，妃爲亞后之名，進同貴妃，以比三司。

translations.literal: Pure Consort had formerly been ranked with the Nine Thorns; as shu means gentle and deferential and fei is the name for one who stands next to the empress, she was advanced to match Honored Consort and compared to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Consort had once been equated with the Nine Ministers; shu denotes warmth and deference, fei the title of one who stands below the empress—she was raised to Honored Consort's level, on a par with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 夫人之號，不殊蕃國。

translations.literal: The title Lady was not different from that of feudatory states.
translations.idiomatic: The title Lady differed in no way from titles used in feudatory states.

sentences.zh: 降淑媛以比九卿。

translations.literal: Pure Lady was lowered to compare with the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Lady was demoted to rank with the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 七年，復置昭容，位在九嬪。

translations.literal: Year 7: Shining Countenance was restored, her place among the Nine Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Shining Countenance was reinstated, with standing among the Nine Consorts.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，太子宮置三內職，良娣比開國侯，保林比五等侯，才人比駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 3: the crown prince's palace established three inner offices—Lady of Excellence ranked with a marquis who founds a state, Guardian of the Grove with a fifth-rank marquis, and Talented Lady with the commandant of horses for the emperor's sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 3 the crown prince's household set up three inner offices: Lady of Excellence, equal to a founding marquis; Guardian of the Grove, to a fifth-rank marquis; and Talented Lady, to the commandant of horses for imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 宣孝陳皇后諱道止，臨淮東陽人，魏司徒陳矯後。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanxiao of the Chen clan, taboo name Daozhi, was a native of Dongyang in Linhuai and a descendant of Chen Jiao, minister of works of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanxiao Chen Daozhi came from Dongyang in Linhuai commandery and was descended from Chen Jiao, minister of works of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父肈之，郡孝廉。

translations.literal: Her father Zhao was a commandery filial and incorrupt candidate.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chen Zhao had been a commandery filial-and-incorrupt nominee.

sentences.zh: 后少家貧，勤織作，家人矜其勞，或止之，后終不改。

translations.literal: In youth the empress's family was poor; she diligently wove and worked. Her kin took pity on her labor and sometimes tried to stop her, but the empress never changed.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor in her girlhood, and she wove and worked without rest. Relatives pitied her toil and tried to make her stop; she never changed her ways.

sentences.zh: 嫁于宣帝，庶生衡陽元王道度、始安貞王道生，后生太祖。

translations.literal: She married Emperor Xuan and bore by concubines Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; afterward she bore the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: She married Emperor Xuan. By concubines he already had Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; afterward she bore Xiao Daocheng, the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖年二歲，乳人乏乳，后夢人以兩甌麻粥與之，覺而乳大出，異而說之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor was two years old, his wet nurse had insufficient milk. The empress dreamed that someone gave her two bowls of hemp porridge; when she awoke her milk flowed freely—she marveled and spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Daocheng was two, his wet nurse could not supply enough milk. The empress dreamed that someone handed her two bowls of hemp porridge; she awoke to find her milk abundant, and she wondered at the omen.

sentences.zh: 宣帝從任在外，后常留家治事教子孫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan was away on assignment; the empress often remained at home to manage affairs and teach the children and grandchildren.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was posted away from home while the empress stayed behind to run the household and instruct the children and grandchildren.

sentences.zh: 有相者謂后曰：「夫人有貴子而不見也。

translations.literal: A physiognomist told the empress: 「My lady has an eminent son, but I have not seen him.
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist told the empress, 「My lady has a son of great rank, yet I have not laid eyes on him.

sentences.zh: 」后歎曰：「我三兒誰當應之。

translations.literal: 」The empress sighed and said: 「Which of my three sons should it be?
translations.idiomatic: 」She sighed. 「I have three sons—which of them can it be?

sentences.zh: 」呼太祖小字曰：「正應是汝耳。

translations.literal: 」She called the Grand Ancestor by his childhood name and said: 「It must be you after all.
translations.idiomatic: 」She called Xiao Daocheng by his childhood name Doujiang and said, 「It must be you.

sentences.zh: 」宣帝殂後，后親自執勤，婢使有過誤，恕不問也。

translations.literal: 」After Emperor Xuan died, the empress personally took charge of labor; when maidservants erred, she forgave them and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: 」After Emperor Xuan's death she herself saw to the work of the household; when maidservants blundered, she pardoned them without question.

sentences.zh: 太祖雖從官，而家業本貧，爲建康令時，高宗等冬月猶無縑纊，而奉膳甚厚，后每撤去兼肉，曰：「於我過足矣。

translations.literal: Though the Grand Ancestor held office, the family estate was originally poor; when he was magistrate of Jiankang, Gaozong and the others in winter still lacked silk padding, yet the meals sent were very rich—the empress each time removed the extra meat and said: 「For me this is more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiao Daocheng held office, the family had always been poor. When he was magistrate of Jiankang, Gaozong and the others still went without padded silk in winter, while the food sent in was lavish—the empress would remove the extra meat and say, 「For me this is already too much.

sentences.zh: 」殂于縣舍，年七十三。

translations.literal: 」She died at the magistrate's quarters, age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: 」She died in the magistrate's quarters, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，追贈竟陵公國太夫人，蜜印，畫青綬，祠以太牢。

translations.literal: Shengming year 3: posthumous enfeoffment as Grand Lady of the state of the Duke of Jingling, with honey seal and painted green cord; sacrifice with the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year 3 she was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Lady of the Duke of Jingling's state, with honey seal and painted green cord, and honored with the great offering.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，追尊孝皇后。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 1: posthumous elevation as Empress Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 she was posthumously honored as Empress Xiao.

sentences.zh: 贈外祖父肈之金紫光祿大夫，謚曰敬侯。

translations.literal: Her maternal grandfather Zhao was given the post of household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chen Zhao was made household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumously titled Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 后母胡氏爲永昌縣靖君。

translations.literal: The empress's mother, the Hu clan, was made Village Lady Jing of Yongchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, née Hu, was made Village Lady Jing of Yongchang county.

sentences.zh: 高昭劉皇后諱智容，廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Empress Gaozhao of the Liu clan, taboo name Zhirong, was a native of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gaozhao Liu Zhirong came from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 祖玄之，父壽之，竝員外郎。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Xuanzhi and father Shouzhi were both supernumerary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Liu Xuanzhi and father Liu Shouzhi had both served as supernumerary gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 武穆裴皇后諱惠昭，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wumu of the Pei clan, taboo name Huizhao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wumu Pei Huizhao came from Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖朴之，給事中。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Puzhi was a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Pei Puzhi had been a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 父璣之，左軍參軍。

translations.literal: Her father Jizhi was a left-army aide.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Pei Jizhi had been a left-army aide.

sentences.zh: 舊顯陽、昭陽二殿，太后、皇后所居也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xianyang and Zhaoyang halls were where the empress dowager and empress dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianyang and Zhaoyang halls had long been the residences of empress dowager and empress.

sentences.zh: 永明中無太后、皇后，羊貴嬪居昭陽殿西，范貴妃居昭陽殿東，寵姬荀昭華居鳳華柏殿。

translations.literal: In Yongming there was neither empress dowager nor empress; Noble Consort Yang dwelt west of Zhaoyang Hall, Honored Consort Fan east of Zhaoyang Hall, and the favored lady Xun Zhaohua in the Phoenix Splendor Cypress Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era there was no empress dowager or empress: Noble Consort Yang lived west of Zhaoyang Hall, Honored Consort Fan to the east, and the favored Xun Zhaohua in the Phoenix Splendor Cypress Hall.

sentences.zh: 宮內御所居壽昌畫殿南閣，置白鷺鼓吹二部；

translations.literal: At the south gallery of the Shouchang Painted Hall, where the emperor dwelt within the palace, two companies of egret-reed pipes were installed;
translations.idiomatic: In the south gallery of the Shouchang Painted Hall, the emperor's inner quarters, two companies of egret-reed pipes were stationed;

sentences.zh: 乾光殿東西頭，置鍾磬兩廂：皆宴樂處也。

translations.literal: at the east and west ends of Qianguang Hall, bell and chime galleries on either side: all were places for feasting and music.
translations.idiomatic: at the east and west ends of Qianguang Hall, bell and stone galleries on either flank—all were halls for feasting and music.

sentences.zh: 上數遊幸諸苑囿，載宮人從後車，宮內深隱，不聞端門鼓漏聲，置鍾於景陽樓上，宮人聞鍾聲，早起裝飾，至今此鍾唯應五鼓及三鼓也。

translations.literal: The emperor often toured the parks and enclosures, carrying palace women in the rear carriage. Deep within the palace one did not hear the drum and water-clock at the Duan Gate; a bell was set on Jingyang Tower. When palace women heard the bell they rose early to dress and adorn themselves—to this day that bell answers only the fifth watch and the third watch.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often toured the royal parks with palace women in the train behind his carriage. Deep inside the palace the drum and clepsydra at the Duan Gate could not be heard, so a bell was hung on Jingyang Tower. At its stroke the women rose early to dress—to this day it sounds only at the fifth watch and the third.

sentences.zh: 車駕數幸琅邪城，宮人常從，早發至湖北埭，雞始鳴。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage often visited Langya walled town; palace women regularly followed. They set out early and reached Hubei ferry landing when the cock first crowed.
translations.idiomatic: The court often went to Langya walled town, palace women in attendance. They left at first light and reached Hubei landing at the first cockcrow.

sentences.zh: 吳郡韓藺英，婦人有文辭。

translations.literal: Han Linying of Wu commandery was a woman of literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Linying of Wu commandery was a woman of literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武世，獻中興賦，被賞入宮。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Xiaowu of Song she presented the "Zhongxing Rhapsody" and, prized, was brought into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Song she submitted the "Rhapsody on Restoration" and, rewarded, was admitted to the palace.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝世，用爲宮中職僚。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Ming of Song she was employed as a palace staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Song she served on the palace staff.

sentences.zh: 世祖以爲博士，教六宮書學，以其年老多識，呼爲「韓公」。

translations.literal: Shizong made her a erudite to teach the six palaces calligraphy and learning; because she was old and knew much, they called her 「Lord Han.」
translations.idiomatic: Shizong appointed her erudite to instruct the six palaces in writing and learning; in her great age and wide knowledge they called her 「Lord Han.」

sentences.zh: 文安王皇后諱寶明，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wen'an of the Wang clan, taboo name Baoming, was a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen'an Wang Baoming came from Linyi in Langya commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖韶之，吳興太守。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Shaozhi was administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Wang Shaozhi had been administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父曄之，太宰祭酒。

translations.literal: Her father Yezhi was libationer of the grand minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wang Yezhi had been libationer to the grand minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王何妃名婧英，廬江灊人，撫軍將軍戢之女也。

translations.literal: Consort He of Prince Yulin, personal name Jingying, was a native of Qian in Lujiang and the daughter of General Who Pacifies the Army He Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Consort He Jingying of Prince Yulin came from Qian in Lujiang commandery and was the daughter of General Who Pacifies the Army He Ji.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，納爲南郡王妃。

translations.literal: Yongming year 2: she was received as consort to the Prince of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 2 she entered the household as consort to the Prince of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一年，爲皇太孫妃。

translations.literal: Year 11: she became consort to the heir apparent of the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 she became consort to the heir apparent of the imperial grandson.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王卽位，爲皇后。

translations.literal: When Prince Yulin took the throne, she became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yulin acceded, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 嫡母劉氏爲高昌縣都鄉君，所生母宋氏，爲餘杭廣昌鄉君。

translations.literal: Her formal mother, the Liu clan, was made Chief Village Lady of Duxiang in Gaochang county; her birth mother, the Song clan, Village Lady of Guangchang in Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Her foster mother, née Liu, was made Chief Village Lady of Duxiang in Gaochang county; her birth mother, née Song, Village Lady of Guangchang in Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 將拜，鏡在牀無故墮地。

translations.literal: As the investiture approached, a mirror on the bed fell to the floor for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of her investiture a mirror on the bed fell to the floor without cause.

sentences.zh: 其冬，與太后同日謁太廟。

translations.literal: That winter she and the empress dowager on the same day paid homage at the Great Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That winter she and the empress dowager visited the Great Temple on the same day.

sentences.zh: 后稟性淫亂，爲妃時，便與外人姦通。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature licentious; even as a consort she had illicit relations with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was wanton by nature; even as a princess consort she took lovers from outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 在後宮，復通帝左右楊珉之，與同寢處如伉儷。

translations.literal: In the inner palace she again had relations with Yang Minzhi, an attendant at the emperor's side, sharing bed and board like man and wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the inner quarters she took up with Yang Minzhi, a favorite at the emperor's side, and they slept and lived together like husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 珉之又與帝相愛褻，故帝恣之。

translations.literal: Minzhi was also on intimate terms with the emperor, so the emperor indulged them.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi was likewise intimate with the emperor, and the emperor let them have their way.

sentences.zh: 迎后親戚入宮，賞賜人百數十萬。

translations.literal: She brought the empress's kinsmen into the palace and bestowed rewards in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned the empress's kin into the palace and lavished rewards running into hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 以世祖耀靈殿處后家屬。

translations.literal: Shizu's Yaoling Hall was given over to house the empress's family.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's Yaoling Hall was set aside to lodge the empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 帝被廢，后貶爲王妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor was deposed, the empress was demoted to princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was deposed, the empress was reduced to princess consort.

sentences.zh: 海陵王王妃名韶明，琅邪臨沂人，太常慈女也。

translations.literal: The consort of the Prince of Hailing was named Shaoming, a native of Linyi in Langya, daughter of Grand Master of Ceremonies Ci.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of the prince of Hailing, named Shaoming, came from Linyi in Langya commandery and was the daughter of Grand Master of Ceremonies Ci.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，納爲臨汝公夫人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming she was taken as Lady of the Lord of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming she was married to the lord of Linru as his lady.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，爲新安王妃。

translations.literal: When Yulin acceded, she became princess consort of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin took the throne, she became princess consort of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，爲皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing she was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing she was raised to empress.

sentences.zh: 其年，降爲海陵王妃。

translations.literal: That same year she was demoted to consort of the Prince of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: That same year she was reduced to consort of the prince of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 明敬劉皇后諱惠端，彭城人，光祿大夫道弘孫也。

translations.literal: Empress Mingjing Liu, personal name Huiduan, was a native of Pengcheng and granddaughter of Household Minister Daohong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mingjing Liu, whose personal name was Huiduan, came from Pengcheng and was the granddaughter of Household Minister Liu Daohong.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲高宗納之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor secured her in marriage for Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor arranged her marriage to Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，除西昌侯夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan she was invested as Lady of the Marquis of Xichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyuan she was made lady to the marquis of Xichang.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，卒，葬江乘縣張山。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming she died and was buried at Zhang Mountain in Jiangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongming she died and was buried at Zhang Mountain in Jiangcheng county.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，贈宣城王妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing she was posthumously given the title Princess Consort of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing she was posthumously titled princess consort of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 高宗卽位，追尊爲敬皇后。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong acceded, she was posthumously honored as Empress Jing.

sentences.zh: 贈父通直郎景猷金紫光祿大夫，母王氏平陽鄉君。

translations.literal: Her father Jingyou, General of Transmission who was Regular, was posthumously made Household Minister with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord; her mother, Lady Wang, was made Lady of Pingyang township.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jingyou, a regular attendant in the transmission office, was posthumously made household minister with the golden seal and purple cord; her mother, Lady Wang, was made lady of Pingyang township.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，高宗崩，改葬，祔于興安陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, when Gaozong died, she was reburied and consigned to Xing'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, when Gaozong died, she was reinterred and laid beside him in Xing'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 東昏褚皇后名令璩，河南陽翟人，太常澄女也。

translations.literal: Empress Chu of Dong Hun, named Lingque, was a native of Yangdi in Henan and daughter of Grand Master of Ceremonies Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Chu of Dong Hun, named Lingque, came from Yangdi in Henan commandery and was the daughter of Grand Master of Ceremonies Chu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，納爲皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu she was taken as the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu she was married to the crown prince as his consort.

sentences.zh: 明年，謁敬后廟。

translations.literal: The following year she paid worship at Empress Jing's temple.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she worshipped at Empress Jing's temple.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，爲皇后。

translations.literal: When Dong Hun acceded, she was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Hun took the throne, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 帝寵潘妃，后不被遇。

translations.literal: The emperor favored Consort Pan; the empress received no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on Consort Pan, and the empress went unvisited.

sentences.zh: 黃淑儀生太子誦，東昏廢，竝爲庶人。

translations.literal: Honored Lady Huang bore Crown Prince Song; when Dong Hun was deposed, both became commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Lady Huang had borne Crown Prince Song; when Dong Hun was deposed, mother and son were both reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 和帝王皇后名蕣華，琅邪臨沂人，太尉儉孫也。

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Emperor He, named Shunhua, was a native of Linyi in Langya and granddaughter of Grand Commandant Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang of Emperor He, named Shunhua, came from Linyi in Langya commandery and was the granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 初爲隨王妃。

translations.literal: At first she was princess consort of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was princess consort of Sui.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，爲皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing she was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing she was raised to empress.

sentences.zh: 帝禪位，后降爲妃。

translations.literal: When the emperor abdicated the throne, the empress was demoted to consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor yielded the throne, the empress was reduced to consort.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：后妃之德，著自風謠，義起閨房，而道化天下。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The virtue of empresses and consorts is recorded in folk song; righteousness rises in the inner chamber and transforms the realm beneath Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The virtue of empresses and consorts shines in folk song; their righteousness begins behind closed doors and spreads until it reshapes the world.

sentences.zh: 繰盆獻種，罔非耕織，佩管晨興，與子同事，可以光熙閫業，作儷公侯。

translations.literal: Reeling the cocoon-tray and offering seed—all is spinning and weaving; girding the shuttle-gauge and rising at dawn, sharing toil with their sons—they can brighten the household estate and stand as peers to dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: They reel the cocoon basin and offer seed—nothing but spinning and weaving; they gird the reed and rise at dawn, working beside their sons—thus the inner household glows and they stand as equals to dukes and marquises.

sentences.zh: 孝、昭二后，竝有賢明之訓，不得母臨萬國。

translations.literal: Empresses Xiao and Gao both possessed wise and clarifying instruction, yet could not mother the myriad domains.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao and Gao empresses both bore wise instruction, yet never ruled the realm as mothers of the state.

sentences.zh: 寶命方昌，椒庭虛位，有婦人焉，空慕周興，禎符顯瑞，徒萃徽名。

translations.literal: While the precious mandate flourished anew, the pepper courts stood empty; certain women only yearned in vain for the Zhou revival—auspicious tokens and bright omens gathered nothing but empty glory.
translations.idiomatic: While the sacred mandate was rising, the empress's courts stood vacant; some women only dreamed of a Zhou restoration—bright omens and lucky signs heaped up nothing but hollow fame.

sentences.zh: 若使掖作同休，陰教遠燮，則馬、鄧風流，復存乎此。

translations.literal: Had the lateral palaces shared one repose and the inner teaching harmonized the realm from afar, the grace of Ma and Deng might have lived here again.
translations.idiomatic: Had the side palaces rested in one accord and the women's teaching steadied the realm from within, the elegance of the Ma and Deng empresses might have returned here.

sentences.zh: 太祖創命，宮禁貶約，毀宋明之紫極，革前代之踰奢，衣不文繡，色無紅采，永巷貧空，有同素室。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor founded the dynasty, palace bounds were stripped back: he destroyed Emperor Ming of Song's Purple Ultimate, reformed past dynasties' excess; robes bore no brocade patterns, colors no scarlet; the long alleys were poor and bare as undecorated rooms.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Progenitor's founding, the palace was pared to austerity: he razed Emperor Ming of Song's Purple Ultimate Hall and cut the extravagance of earlier reigns—garments without figured embroidery, colors without red; the long alleys were empty and poor as plain chambers.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，運藉休平，壽昌前興，鳳華晚搆，香柏文檉，花梁繡柱，雕金鏤寶，頗用房帷，趙瑟吳趨，承閑奏曲，歲費傍恩，足使充牣，事由私蓄，無損國儲。

translations.literal: When Shizu succeeded, fortune rode on peaceful times—Shouchang built early, Fenghua raised late; fragrant cypress and patterned beams, floral rafters and embroidered pillars, carved gold and inset jewels filled the curtained chambers; Zhao harps and Wu airs were played in leisure; yearly spending from ancillary favor was enough to overflow the stores—all from private hoards, never draining the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu succeeded, the age rested on peace—Shouchang rose early, Fenghua late; fragrant cypress and patterned rafters, painted beams and embroidered pillars, carved gold and set gems crowded the curtained halls; Zhao zithers and Wu songs filled idle hours; yearly outlays from side revenues overflowed the vaults—paid from private stores, never touching the state coffers.

sentences.zh: 高宗仗數矯情，外行儉陋，內奉宮業，曾莫云改。

translations.literal: Gaozong leaned on numerology and feigned restraint: outwardly frugal and plain, inwardly he sustained palace industry and never spoke of change.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong trusted omens and played at austerity—plain and mean in public, yet he kept the palace estate as before and never breathed a word of reform.

sentences.zh: 東昏喪道，侈風大扇，銷糜海內，以贍浮飾，哲婦傾城，同符殷、夏。

translations.literal: Dong Hun lost the Way; extravagance swept wide; he melted the realm to feed vain ornament—sagacious women overturned cities, matching Yin and Xia alike.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hun abandoned the Way; luxury blazed across the land; he melted the empire to pay for idle display—wise women toppled cities, in the manner of Yin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 所以垂戒於方來也。

translations.literal: Thus a warning is left to generations yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: So a warning is set down for ages still to come.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宣武孝則，識有先知。

translations.literal: In praise: The Filial Norm of Xuanxiao—her discernment held foresight.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Empress Xuanxiao, filial and correct—she saw what was coming before it came.

sentences.zh: 高昭誕武，世載母儀。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao bore the Martial heir; for generations she carried the motherly pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao bore the martial emperor; her motherly measure passed down the line.

sentences.zh: 裴穆儲閫，位亦從隳。

translations.literal: Pei the Reverent stored the inner palace—and rank followed ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent Pei kept the inner palace—and her station fell with its fall.

sentences.zh: 明敬典冊，配在宗枝。

translations.literal: Mingjing's canon and seals—matched to the imperial branch.
translations.idiomatic: Mingjing's rites and writ—joined to the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 秋宮亦遽，軒景前虧。

translations.literal: The autumn palace too was sudden; the carriage-sun dimmed before its time.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn palace too was cut short; the chariot sun waned before its season.

sentences.zh: 文安廢主，百憂已離，中興秉制，揖讓弘規。

translations.literal: Wen'an's deposed lord, a hundred cares already gone; at Zhongxing she held the regalia, yielding the throne in grand courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an and the deposed sovereign, grief already behind them; at Zhongxing she took the seals, then yielded the throne in great ceremony.

translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.

translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi (January 1972).
